scope: Independent English captions aligned to the five new Korean framing paragraphs after measured narration; all current approved text and PCM are preserved.

scenes.title: A frame's calculation and storage budget
lines: Where should we spend computation and memory to make a sharper image? We will connect shadow pages, temporal upscaling and mobile rendering, in that order. Engine demonstrations and small numerical examples will help us follow the tradeoffs, starting with storing only the shadows that are needed.

scenes.title: Costs removed and information still needed
lines: We stored the shadows we needed, reused valid earlier samples and adapted intermediate data to the device. The key is to distinguish the information required from the costs that remain. The next part uses that budget to examine the selection of light paths and light samples.

scenes.title: Lighting and fine detail with few samples
lines: If we cannot calculate every light path, which samples should we choose? We will connect Cyberpunk's path tracing and reconstruction, Unreal's many lights, and thin hair and overlapping surfaces. Comparing actual screen changes with worked examples, we begin with how one path contributes to brightness.

scenes.title: Separate selection from reconstruction
lines: Even after selecting useful paths and lights, samples remain scarce, and thin overlapping surfaces such as hair require more information. We therefore separated visibility from the reconstruction of missing information. The next part connects these results to the final image and to inspection of an actual frame.

scenes.title: How far can we verify the final image?
lines: Can an attractive image tell us how it was calculated? We will distinguish the roles through DLSS5, examine actual exposure and focus demonstrations, then inspect a frame's inputs and outputs. Displayed frames and game calculations have different responsibilities; we begin with what reconstruction is asked to do.
